text: Which of the following is not a correct method of the preparation of benzylamine from cyanobenzene ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
With $\mathrm{SnCl}{}_{2}$ and $\mathrm{HCl}$ (Stephen reduction), $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CN}$ is reduced to the aldimine $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}=\mathrm{NH}$ (as its hydrochloride); $\mathrm{NaBH}{}_{4}$ then reduces the $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{N}$ bond to give $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, so (A) is a valid method.

Catalytic hydrogenation with $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$/Ni, and $\mathrm{LiAlH}{}_{4}$ followed by $\mathrm{H}{}_{3}\mathrm{O}{}^{+}$, both reduce $-\mathrm{C}\equiv \mathrm{N}$ to $-\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{NH}{}_{2}$, so (B) and (C) give benzylamine.

Aqueous $\mathrm{HCl}$ hydrolyses the nitrile to benzoic acid, $\mathrm{C}{}_{6}\mathrm{H}{}_{5}\mathrm{COOH}$, which $\mathrm{NaBH}{}_{4}$ does not reduce, so (D) gives no benzylamine.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text: The highest possible oxidation states of uranium and plutonium, respectively are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The highest possible oxidation states of uranium and plutonium can be identified by considering the electronic configurations of these elements and noting the number of valence electrons available for bonding.

Uranium (U, atomic number 92) has the electronic configuration: 
$[Rn]5f^{3}6d^{1}7s^{2}$

Plutonium (Pu, atomic number 94) has the electronic configuration: 
$[Rn]5f^{6}7s^{2}$

To find the highest oxidation state, we sum the number of $d$, $f$, and $s$ electrons in the valence shell.

For uranium :

$3(f)+1(d)+2(s)=6$

So the highest oxidation state of uranium is +6.

For plutonium :

$6(f)+2(s)=8$

So the highest oxidation state of plutonium is +8. However, in practice, plutonium is known to exhibit a highest oxidation state of +7.

Comparing with the given options, the correct answer is :

Option D : 6 and 7.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text: In chromatography, which of the following statements is incorrect for $R_{f}$ ?
options: $R_{f}$  value depends on the type of chromatography.

$R_{f}$
 value is dependent on the mobile phase.

The value of $R_{f}$
 can not be more than one.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$R_{f} =$ $\frac{x}{y}$

$x$ = Distance moved by the substance from baseline

$y$ = Distance moved by the solvent from baseline

Option A : Correct. The $R_{f}$ value can depend on the type of chromatography being used because different methods can use different stationary and mobile phases, which can influence how far a substance travels.

Option B : Incorrect. The $R_{f}$ value is actually inversely related to adsorption. A higher Rf value indicates that the substance is less strongly adsorbed to the stationary phase, and therefore moves further along with the mobile phase.

Option C : Correct. The nature of the mobile phase can greatly influence the $R_{f}$ value. The more compatible the substance is with the mobile phase, the further it will travel, leading to a higher Rf value.

Option D : Correct. By definition, the $R_{f}$ value cannot exceed one, as a substance cannot travel further than the solvent.

So, Option B is incorrect for the $R_{f}$ value in chromatography.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text: The INCORRECT statement is :
options: the color of [CoCl$(NH_{3})_{5}$]$^{2+}$ is violet as it absorbs the yellow light.
the gemstone, ruby, has $Cr^{3+}$ ions occupying the octahedral sites of beryl.
the spin-only magnetic moment of [$Ni(NH_{3})_{4}(H_{2}O)_{2}$]$^{2+}$ is 2.83 BM.
the spin-only magnetic moments of [$Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$^{2+}$ and [$Cr(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$^{2+}$ are nearly similar.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
(A) $[\mathrm{CoCl}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{5}]{}^{2+}$ absorbs yellow light (about 535 nm), and the complementary colour violet is observed, so (A) is correct.

(B) Ruby is aluminium oxide (corundum, $\mathrm{Al}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{3}$) in which about 0.5–1% of the octahedral $\mathrm{Al}{}^{3+}$ sites are occupied by $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$ ions; $\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$ in beryl ($\mathrm{Be}{}_{3}\mathrm{Al}{}_{2}\mathrm{Si}{}_{6}\mathrm{O}{}_{18}$) gives emerald. So (B) is incorrect.

(C) In octahedral $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{4}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{2}]{}^{2+}$, $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ is $3d^{8}$ ($t_{2g}^{6}e_{g}^{2}$) with 2 unpaired electrons, so $μ=\sqrt{2(2+2)}=\sqrt{8}=2.83\text{BM}$; (C) is correct.

(D) High-spin $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{6}$, $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$) and high-spin $[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{4}$, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{1}$) each have 4 unpaired electrons, so both have $μ=\sqrt{4(4+2)}=4.90\text{BM}$; (D) is correct.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
For the reaction of $H_{2}$ with $I_{2}$, the rate constant is $2.5 × 10^{–4} dm^{3}$
 mol$^{–1}s^{–1}$
 at 327°C and $1.0 dm^{3}$
 mol$^{–1}s^{–1}$
 at
527°C. The activation energy for the reaction, in kJ mole$^{–1}$
 is : $(R = 8.314 JK^{–1}$
 mol$^{–1}$
)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
From Arrhenius equation, we get

$\log \frac{K_{2}}{K_{1}}=\frac{E_{a}}{2.303R}\left (\frac{1}{T_{1}}-\frac{1}{T_{2}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $\log \frac{1}{2.5\times 10^{-4}}=\frac{E_{a}}{2.303\times 8.314}\left (\frac{1}{600}-\frac{1}{800}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ 3.6 = $\frac{E_{a}}{2.303\times 8.314}\times \frac{200}{600\times 800}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E_{a} = 166 kJ/$mol

text:
The ratio of the shortest wavelength of two spectral series of hydrogen spectrum is found to be about 9. The
spectral series are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Shortest wavelength can be found when $n_{2} =$ $\infty$

$\frac{1}{λ_{shortest}}=RZ^{2}\left \{\frac{1}{n_{1}^{2}}-\frac{1}{\infty ^{2}}\right \}$

Here $n_{1} =$ series number.

$\Rightarrow\frac{1}{λ_{shortest}}=$ $\frac{RZ^{2}}{n_{1}^{2}}$ = $\frac{R(1)^{2}}{n_{1}^{2}}$

$\therefore$ $\frac{λ_{B}}{λ_{A}}=\left (\frac{n_{B}}{n_{A}}\right )^{2}$

Given, $\left (\frac{n_{B}}{n_{A}}\right )^{2}=9$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{n_{B}}{n_{A}}=3$

$\therefore$ Series number of B = 3 $\times$ Series number of A

So,

If series number of A is Lyman( n = 1 )

then series number of B is Paschen( n = 3 ).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
For the reaction,

 $2SO_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g) = 2SO_{3}(g)$, $\Delta$H = –57.2 kJ mol$^{–1}$
 and $K_{C} = 1.7 × 10^{16}$

Which of the following statement is incorrect ?
options: The equilibrium will shift in forward direction as the pressure increase.
The addition of inert gas at constant volume will not affect the equilibrium constant.

The equilibrium constant is large suggestive of reaction going to completion and so no catalyst is
required.
The equilibrium constant decreases as the temperature increase.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For $2~\mathrm{SO}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})+\mathrm{O}{}_{2}(\mathrm{g})2\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}(\mathrm{g})$, $\Delta n_{g}=2-3=-1$, so an increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium forward: (A) is correct.

An equilibrium constant depends only on temperature, and an inert gas added at constant volume leaves every partial pressure unchanged, so neither the equilibrium nor $K$ is affected: (B) is correct.

The reaction is exothermic ($\Delta H<0$), so $K$ decreases as the temperature rises: (D) is correct.

A large $K$ only means that the equilibrium mixture is rich in $\mathrm{SO}{}_{3}$; it says nothing about how fast equilibrium is reached. The reaction is very slow without a catalyst, so $\mathrm{V}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{5}$ is used in the contact process to raise the rate, and a catalyst does not change $K$. Statement (C) is incorrect.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
1 g of a non-volatile non-electrolyte solute is dissolved in 100 g of two different solvents A and B whose
ebullioscopic constants are in the ratio of 1 : 5. The ratio of the elevation in their boiling points, $\frac{\Delta T_{b}(A)}{\Delta T_{b}(B)}$, is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$\frac{(k_{b})_{A}}{(k_{b})_{B}}=\frac{1}{5}$

$\Delta T_{b}(A)=k_{b}(A)\times$ Molality of A

$\Delta T_{b}(B)=k_{b}(B)\times$ Molality of B

Here, Molality of A = Molality of B = m

$\frac{\Delta T_{b}(A)}{\Delta T_{b}(B)}=\frac{(k_{b})_{A}}{(k_{b})_{B}}\times \frac{m}{m}$ = $\frac{1}{5}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
The difference between $\Delta$H and $\Delta$U ($\Delta$H – $\Delta$U), when the combustion of one mole of heptane(l) is carried
out at a temperature T, is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

$\Delta$H - $\Delta$U = $\Delta n_{g}RT$

$C_{7}H_{16}(l) + 11O_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $7CO_{2}(g) + 8H2O(l$)

Here $\Delta n_{g} = 7 - 11 = - 4$

$\therefore$ $\Delta$H - $\Delta$U = - 4RT

text:
The minimum amount of $O_{2}(g)$ consumed per gram of reactant is for the reaction : 
(Given atomic mass : Fe =
56, O = 16, Mg = 24, P = 31, C = 12, H = 1)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$(a) 4Fe(s) + 3O_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $2Fe_{2}O_{3}(s)$

$\frac{MolesofO_{2}}{3}=\frac{MolesofFe}{4}$

$\Rightarrow$ Moles of $O_{2} =$ $\frac{3}{4}$ $\times$ $\frac{1}{56}$ moles = $\frac{3}{224}$ moles = $\frac{3}{224}\times 32$ g of $O_{2} = 0.43 g$ of $O_{2}$

$(b) P_{4}(s) + 5O_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $P_{4}O_{10}(s)$

$\frac{MolesofO_{2}}{5}=\frac{MolesofP_{4}}{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ Moles of $O_{2} = 5$ $\times$ $\frac{1}{124}$ moles = $\frac{1}{24.8}$ moles = $\frac{1}{24.8}\times 32$ g of $O_{2} = 1.3 g$ of $O_{2}$

$(c) C_{3}H_{8}(g) + 5O_{2}(g)$ $\to$ $3CO_{2}(g) + 4H_{2}O(l)$

$\frac{MolesofO_{2}}{5}=\frac{MolesofC_{3}H_{8}}{1}$

$\Rightarrow$ Moles of $O_{2} = 5$ $\times$ $\frac{1}{44}$ moles = $\frac{1}{8.8}$ moles = $\frac{1}{8.8}\times 32$ g of $O_{2} = 3.6 g$ of $O_{2}$

$(d) 2Mg(s) + O_{2}(g)$ $\to$ 2MgO(s)

$\frac{MolesofO_{2}}{1}=\frac{MolesofMg}{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ Moles of $O_{2} =$ $\frac{1}{2}$ $\times$ $\frac{1}{24}$ moles = $\frac{1}{48}$ moles = $\frac{1}{48}\times 32$ g of $O_{2} = 0.66 g$ of $O_{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text:
The pH of $a 0.02 M NH_{4}Cl$ solution will be :

 [given $K_{b} (NH_{4}OH) = 10^{–5}$
 and log 2 = 0.301]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$NH_{4}^{+} + H_{2}O$  ⇋ $NH_{4}OH + H^{+}$

[$H^{+}$] = c$α$

= $\sqrt{k_{a}\left (NH_{4}^{+}\right )\times c}$

= $\sqrt{\frac{k_{w}}{k_{b}(NH_{4}OH)}\times c}$

= $\sqrt{\frac{10^{-14}}{10^{-5}}\times 0.02}$

= $\sqrt{20}\times 10^{-6}$

$\therefore$ pH = $-\log \left (\sqrt{20}\times 10^{-6}\right )$ = 5.35
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text: The crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE) of [$Fe(H_{2}O)_{6}$]$Cl_{2}$ and $K_{2}$[NiCl$_{4}$] respectively, are :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}){}_{6}]\mathrm{Cl}{}_{2}$, iron is $\mathrm{Fe}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{6}$) in an octahedral field of weak-field $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$, so it is high spin, $t_{2g}^{4}e_{g}^{2}$.

$\text{CFSE}=4(-0.4\Delta _{o})+2(+0.6\Delta _{o})=-0.4\Delta _{o}$

In $\mathrm{K}{}_{2}[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]$, $[\mathrm{NiCl}{}_{4}]{}^{2-}$ is tetrahedral with $\mathrm{Ni}{}^{2+}$ ($3d^{8}$). In a tetrahedral field the $e$ set lies lower ($-0.6\qquad \Delta _{t}$ per electron) and the $t_{2}$ set higher ($+0.4\qquad \Delta _{t}$ per electron), giving $e^{4}t_{2}^{4}$.

$\text{CFSE}=4(-0.6\Delta _{t})+4(+0.4\Delta _{t})=-0.8\Delta _{t}$

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

text: Which one of the following graphs between molar conductivity ($\Lambda _{m}$) versus $\sqrt{C}$ is correct ?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The graph is drawn using following equation,

$\Lambda _{m}=\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }-b\sqrt{c}$

As the size of $K^{+}$ is higher than the size of $Na^{+}$, then the hydration radii of aqueous $Na^{+}$ will be more than the aqueous $K^{+}$. Therefore the ionic mobility of $Na^{+}$ will be smaller than $K^{+}$. Hence the conductance of $K^{+}$ will be higher.

 $\therefore$ $\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }$ of $K^{+} >$ $\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }$ of $Na^{+}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }$(KCl) > $\Lambda _{m}^{\infty }$(NaCl)

So, y intercept is more for KCl.

As slope b is constant both the lines will be parallel.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 10th April Evening Slot

The increasing order of nucleophilicity of the following nucleophiles is :

$(a) CH_{3}CO_{2}^{-}$           $(b) H_{2}O$

Stability order :

$H_{2}O > CH_{3}SO_{3}^{-} > CH_{3}CO_{2}^{-} >$ $O^{-}H$

So Nucleophilicity order :

$H_{2}O < CH_{3}SO_{3}^{-} < CH_{3}CO_{2}^{-} <$ $O^{-}H$
